newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl - German prospects good, backs EMU timetable.
newsitem.headline: Kohl - German prospects good, backs EMU timetable.

text.p: German chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday that the German economy had a good basis for growth and that he intended to stick by the timetable and entry criteria for European monetary union.
In a summary of a speech to industrialists issued by the chancellery, Kohl said that Germany had an excellent basis to continue to belong to the league of top industrial nations.
"Low interest rates, virtual price stability and a lively global economy mean that the spring recovery is standing on a firm foundation," he said.
He added however that unemoplyment was too high and said Germany had more work to do to create the conditions for new jobs.
Kohl called 1997 the key year for European security and for closer union between European Union states.
Commenting on Europe's planned single currency he said that he "stands by both the stability criteria in the Maastricht Treaty as well as the timetable".
EMU is due to start in 1999 grouping those nations which meet economic targets laid down in the Maastricht treaty.
